key_insight: Severe plastic deformation of CrMnFeCoNi increases both electrical and thermal conductivity despite introducing dense defects, with atomic-scale disorder changes proposed as the cause.
engineering_relevance: Defect engineering may offer a route to combine high hardness with improved charge and heat transport in high-entropy alloys.
method: Apply high-pressure torsion for up to 4 turns to generate hierarchical defects and nanostructure.
Characterize hardness, electrical and thermal transport, heat capacity, and thermal expansion.
Use Wiedemann–Franz analysis and the Cahill–Pohl model to interpret heat transport.
evidence_signal: After 4 turns, electrical conductivity rises from 0.953 to 1.003 ± 0.005 MS/m and thermal conductivity from 10.3 to 14.4 W/(m·K), with estimated electron and phonon contributions increasing by approximately 5% and 100%, respectively.
watch_item: Deformation-induced short-range ordering remains a hypothesized mechanism rather than an established cause of the transport enhancement.
paper_title: Unusual increase in electrical and thermal conductivity of severely deformed CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy: Roles of disordering and nanostructuring in electron and phonon transport
